dataset.name: clothing-dataset-small
dataset.author: Alexey Grigorev
dataset.description: Pre-split (train/validation/test) subset covering the 10 most common classes from the larger clothing-dataset-full (5,000+ real photographed clothing images). We use the small subset because it is small enough to train quickly in Colab, already split by the dataset author, and requires no Kaggle account/API key — just a plain git clone.
dataset.verification_method: Confirmed directly against the repository's live file listing via the GitHub API (repos/alexeygrigorev/clothing-dataset-small/contents and .../contents/train) before writing this mapping, rather than assumed from memory.

mapping_notes.Tops: 3 source classes merged (t-shirt, shirt, longsleeve) — likely the best-represented VISTIQ category.
mapping_notes.Outerwear: Only 'outwear' maps here — a single source class, likely one of the smaller ones. Check its actual image count during dataset inspection before trusting the model's Outerwear predictions.
mapping_notes.Dresses: Only 'dress' maps here — a direct 1:1 mapping.
mapping_notes.Footwear: Only 'shoes' maps here — a direct 1:1 mapping. Note this dataset does not distinguish sneakers/sandals/boots.
mapping_notes.Accessories: Only 'hat' maps here — a single, narrow source class. The trained model's notion of 'Accessories' will effectively only mean 'hat-like' images; it will not recognize bags, jewelry, belts, etc. This is a real, documented limitation of this dataset choice, not something to paper over.
mapping_notes.unmapped_dataset_labels: None — every one of the 10 source folders maps to exactly one VISTIQ category, so no images need to be dropped for label reasons.

color_palette.note: Used by ml/inference/color.py for deterministic (non-ML) dominant-color bucketing — not related to the category classifier.
